class.name: AudioEffectSNESEcho
class.brief_description: The SNES S-DSP echo: a delay ring, an 8-tap FIR filter and feedback, bit-exact at 32 kHz.
class.description: Emulates the echo unit of the SNES sound chip. The echo path is resampled to 32 kHz, run with the hardware's 16-bit integer arithmetic (wrapping multiplies, saturating additions, 15-bit samples), and resampled back. The dry path stays at the mix rate. Properties take the hardware register values, so presets from SNES games copy over directly. The whole output, dry and wet, is delayed by about 2.5 ms so the two stay aligned, and the final mix saturates at full scale as the hardware does.

method.name: set_fir_coefficient
method.description: Sets FIR coefficient [param tap] (0-7), clamped to -128..127.

members.member: Left dry volume (MVOLL), -128..127. 127 is unity; negative inverts phase.
Echo length (EDL) in 16 ms blocks, 0..15. 0 is a one-sample ring. As on hardware, a change takes effect only when the ring next wraps.
Echo feedback (EFB), -128..127: how much of the FIR output is written back into the ring.
Whether new audio is written into the ring (FLG bit 5 clear). Disabling it freezes the ring's contents, which keep repeating.
FIR0, the coefficient on the oldest of the 8 samples, -128..127. 127 on one tap with the rest 0 passes the echo through at about unity gain.
FIR7, the coefficient on the newest sample, -128..127.
